records.qn_text:

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA)

(a) to (c) Health Melas have been organised in Mathura (17-20 September, 2000), Delhi (16-25 October, 2000), Kargil (21-25 October, 2000) and Patna (19-21 November, 2000) with a view to provisioning integrated quality health care services, to meet the unmet needs among all segments of population. In these melas people become aware of a number of options before them in terms of the different systems of medicine (allopathy, homeopathy, ayurveda and unani). People begin to comprehend the linkages between preventive, promotive, curative and rehabilitative health care and also the linkages between the primary, secondary and tertiary health sectors. People are getting sensitised to the role of Central Government, the State Government, the elected local bodies, the NGOs and the professional organisations. The pre-mela demographic and epidemiologial surveys provide vast amounts of data about a given city and its rural hinterland. The State Government did not consider it advisable to hold the mela in October/November, 2000 as the State was goving through election to local bodies. The `Health and Family Welfare Mela` is proposed to be organised at Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh from 31st January to 2nd February, 2001. records.qtitle: INCOME TAX COLLECTION FROM WINNERS AND ORGANISERS OF KAUN BANEGA CROREPATI. OIH
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are collecting Income Tax on the amount won by winners in the most popular programme `Kaun Banega Crorepati`.

(b) if so, the percentage amount of income tax;

(c) whether Government have collected Income Tax from the sponsors and producers of the said programme; if so, the amount collected separately from sponsors and producers; and

(d) if not, the reasons and purpose for not collecting Income Tax from sponsors and producers of the programme.
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI GINGEE N. RAMACHANDRAN)


(a) & (b):- The amount won by winners in the programme `Kaun Banega Crorepati` is taxable @ 40% plus sur-charge under Section 115BB of the Income-tax Act, 1961. However, there is no provision for deduction of tax at source on such winnings.
(c) & (d):- The producers of the said programme are regular corporate assessees and are assessed to tax over the years. Since the programme has started only in the current financial year, income and tax thereon from this will be known only after the Return of Income for the relevant period i.e. Assessment Year 2001-02 is filed which will be due on 30th November, 2001.
Further, the sponsors are well known companies and are all asessed to tax. However, these sponsors who are advertising on TV programme are only incurring expenditure. Since there is no income involved, there is no tax liability in the case of sponsors.

THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING

(SMT. SUSHMA SWARAJ)

(a) to (c) : No Sir. Prasar Bharati has intimated that M/s Nine M/s Network Australia Pty Ltd. has been awarded contract for telecasting certain programmes on DD-2 channel for the 7.00 PM to 9.00 PM slot after they made the highest bid for the said slot offering a bid amount of Rs. 59.00 crores against the floor price fixed at Rs. 55.00 crores. The same company through M/s Nine Broadcasting India Private Ltd. has also been granted the 9.00 PM to 10.00 PM slot for DD-2 after they successfully quoted the a bid of Rs. 62.00 crores against the Floor price of Rs. 42.5 crores fixed for the said slot. The programmes are also being repeated on the following day, morning transmission of DD-2, from 9.00 AM to 12.00 Noon.
Prasar Bharati has also intimated that M/s Nine Network of Australia has also been awarded a contract for production of live signals of international cricket events to be held in India, for international production companies, after the bid for the said production was found best, economical and suitable by Prasar Bharati after proper evaluation.
During presently ongoing examination by the Standing Committee on Information & Technology about functioning of Prasar Bharati, issue of agreement with M/s Nine Network, Australia, has also come up but as yet Standing Committee on Information Technology has not given any report objecting to this decision of Prasar Bharati.

records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav

(b) whether efforts are being made to expel the Indian teachers teaching in the said schools;

(c) if so, whether any initiatives have been taken/are being taken by Government to maintain the status-quo for these Indian teachers; and

(d) if so, the outcome thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI JASWANT SINGH)


(a) to (d) A Statement is placed on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN PARTS (A) TO (D) OF THE ANSWER TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 78 TO BE ANSWER ON 23.11.2000 ON `INDIAN TEACHER IN NEPALI SCHOOLS`.
In view of non-availability of full information or records in this regard, precise estimates of the number of Indian citizens working as teachers in the schools of Nepal is not possible. The government, however, work on the basis of a figure approximately of 1000 plus, as a guide.
The Government of India is not aware of any attempts to remove Indian teachers from their jobs. However, a majority of the Indian teachers have not been granted permanent status so far, they continue to work on an ad hoc and temporary contractual basis, which deprives them of facilities such as provident fund, increments, pension, voluntary retirement benefits, promotion, medical reimbursement, etc., benefits that are available to their Nepalese counterparts.
The issue of regularisation of service of the Indian teachers in Nepal has been discussed on a number of occasions between the Government of India and His Majesty`s Government of Nepal, including at the highest level. During the visit of the Prime Minister of Nepal to India in June 1990, it was agreed that the Indian nationals employed in schools in Nepal would be placed on the same footing as Nepalese nationals as regards the terms and conditions of employment. This assurance has been reiterated by the Nepalese side during subsequent high-level exchanges as well.
In 1990-91, the Nepalese Cabinet had decided that as a one-time exception, all teachers who were working for at least five years in various Government schools till the previous year, would be made permanent. In accordance with this decision, it is estimated that about 100 Indian teachers were made permanent. In 1998, His Majesty`s Government of Nepal issued a notification whereby the Indian teachers working in Nepalese schools, who have completed one year of service by 1990-1991 and have still been working on temporary basis, would not be removed on the basis of nationality alone. The notification also stated that those teachers who would like to retire or who voluntarily quit their position or who were removed for reasons other than nationality, shall be granted a lumpsum benefit depending on their length of service.
The issue was again raised with the Prime Minister of Nepal, Mr. G.P. Koirala, during his visit to India in August 2000. A Joint Press Statement issued on August 3, 2000 during the visit stated that His Majesty`s Government would implement the decisions taken in 1998 in this regard. Meanwhile, the Government of India continues to take up specific problems of the Indian teachers with His Majesty`s Government of Nepal through diplomatic channels.

records.qtitle: KITH AND KIN OF KARGIL MARTYRS .
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that kith and kin of Kargil war martyrs have been facing hardships due to carelessness on the part of Government;

(b) if not, whether Government’s assurance given in respect of Kargil martyrs has been fulfilled;

(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and

(d) the assistance given by Government to the kith and kin of Kargil martyrs of Bihar, facing hardships?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES)


(a) to (d): A statement is attached.


STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 255 FOR 22.11.2000 REGARDING KITH AND KIN OF KARGIL MARTYRS.


The Government has taken adequate care of the kith and kin of Kargil war martyrs, including those, belonging to Bihar. A comprehensive package of benefits for the next of kin of all casualties of Kargil Operation has been implemented. The details are as under:
I. Benefits given by the Government to the next of kin of Kargil casualties, who applied for these benefits to the Government:

(a) Ex-gratia amount: Rs. 10.00 lakhs

(b) Liberalised Family Pension equal to the last pay drawn by the deceased.

(c) Death-cum-retirement Gratuity, as admissible

(d) under the Rules. Army Group Insurance Scheme:

(i) Officers Rs. 8 lakhs

(ii)JCOs/ORs – Rs. 3.75 lakhs
II. Benefits given to the next of kin from the National Defence Fund:

(i) Housing: Rs. 5 lakhs to each family of the Armed Forces personnel killed and the personnel invalided out of service, for acquiring a dwelling unit or for making additions/alterations/renovations to the existing unit.

(ii Education: A lump sum grant of Rs. 1 lakh per ) child or Rs. 2 lakhs per family for children’s education.

(ii Parents: Dependent parents of the deceased
i) soldiers are to be paid monthly interest accruing from a fixed deposit of Rs. 2.00 lakhs each.
III. Assistance from Army Central Welfare Fund:
Each next of kin of the Armed Forces personnel, killed in Kargil operation, has been given Rs. 30,000 from this Fund.
Families of all Kargil martyrs have been given the entitled financial and other benefits after completion of necessary formalities.
IV. Allotment of Oil Product Agencies:
A special scheme for direct allotment of 500 oil product agencies to the next of kin of those, killed in Kargil operation, was announced. Under this Scheme, 451 applications were received. Out of this, 382 Petrol Pumps/LPG dealerships have been approved for allotment to widows/NoK of those, killed in Kargil Operation. The remaining cases are in progress.
In, so far as, Bihar is concerned, 16 Service personnel were killed during Kargil Operation. Widows/Next of Kin of 15 personnel have been allotted Petrol Pumps/LPG dealerships. The case of one person, which was received late, is under consideration.
V. Benefits given by the State Government of Bihar:
The State Government of Bihar announced an ex- gratia payment of Rs. 10 lakhs to Kargil casualties belonging to Bihar.

records.ans_text:
MINISTER FOR RAILWAYS


(KUMARI MAMTA BANERJEE)


(a) to (b) A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) AND (b) OF STARRED QUESTION No. 444 BY PROF. RAM GOPAL YADAV AND SHRI RAMA SHANKER KAUSHIK TO BE ANSWERED IN RAJYA SABHA ON 25.8.2000 REGARDING MOLESTATION BY GRP JAWANS.

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) According to Entry No. 2 of the State List of the Constitution of India, `Police` (including Railway and Village police), is a state subject. Prevention of crime, registration of cases, their investigation and maintenance of law and order in Railway premises as well as on the running trains is the Constitutional responsibility of the State Government concerned which they discharge through their Government Railway Police

(GRP). Therefore, the report in this case was asked for from the GRP, Haryana.

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY ( SHRI MURASOLI MARAN)

(a) to (c) No export or import can be made by any person or company without an Importer-Exporter Code (IEC) Number. An Importer-Exporter Code Number is granted, on application, by the competent authority in accordance with the procedure specified in Export Import Policy, Handbook of Procedures, Vol.I. If there is any non resident interest in the applicant firm and non resident investment has been made with repatriation benefit, the IEC Code Number is granted only after ascertaining that the firm has obtained necessary approval from Reserve Bank of India.
Once a foreign company has been granted IEC Number, the export and import to be made by the company shall be subject to all the provisions of Export and Import Policy, as applicable on any other company including domestic companies.

No tuition fee has been increased during the last one year except in the case of Kendriya Vidyalayas in project sector which are financed by sponsoring agencies where they have been permitted to prescribe such scale of fees as they may consider appropriate from the academic session 2000-2001. 1.4.2000 with a view to facilitate carrying out of various students activities and increase in total amount is nominal. There is no proposal at present for withdrawal of the said orders.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a),(b),(c),(d) AND (e) RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.196 FOR 4/8/2000 REGARDING NUMBER OF SPECIES/SUB- SPECIES OF PLANTS AND WILD ANIMALS BY SHRI RAMA SHANKAR KAUSHIK AND PROF. RAM GOPAL YADAV

(a), (b), (c), (d) & (e) India has nearly 46000 species of plants and about 81000 species of known fauna. The poaching and illegal trade of the parts and products both from wild plants and animals are one of the major causes of threat to wildlife. State Governments and various Departments of Central Government are making efforts to control the poaching and illegal trade of parts and Producers of wild animals. The list of important seizures made since 1996 is annexed. The list includes two seizures of legs viz. that of Jackal and the birds of prey.
The mandatory provisions regarding punishment for hunting of wild animals and illegal trade in wild animals and plants are quite stringent- In case of hunting of endangered species, the term of Imprisonment may extend up to six: years. The persons indulging in illegal trade of wild animals are punishable for imprisonment which may ex-tend to seven years. There is no upper limit on the fine that the Courts can impose in this regard. There are proposals to make the penalties more stringent.
The punishment in respect of offences related to endangered species of plants may extend to three years imprisonment and fine up to Rs. 25,000/-.

records.qtitle: AMENDMENT OF DELHI UNIVERSITY ACT .
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:

THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI)

records.qtitle: CBI INQUIRY IN THE CASE OF EX CHIEF SECRETARY OF NCTD .
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a) on what basis the CBI interrogated Jal Singh relative of Virender Singh, former Chief Secretary, Delhi Government;

(b) the information relevant to the case derived by CBI from the above inquiry;

(c) whether Jal Singh had died under torture inflicted by CBI; if not, whether Government would conduct any investigation into it and take action against the officers found guilty; and

(d) if so, by when; and if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( CH. VIDYASAGAR RAO )

(a): Shri Jal Singh was examined by the CBI on the basis of source information and facts collected during investigation in the criminal case registered against Shri Virender Singh, former principal Secretary, Training & Technical Education, government of NCT of Delhi.

(b): Shri Jal Singh in the course of his examination disclosed the details of a number of Benami properties allegedly owned by the said Shri Virender Singh.

(c)&(d): Shri Jal Singh was called to the CBI office during the period from 12.05.2000 to 14.05.2000 for the lawful purpose of interrogation and was examined strictly in accordance with law. He was an important witness in the case and had also fully cooperated in the investigation of the case registered against Shri Virender Singh. There was, therefore, no question of causing any harassment to him. The inquiry made into the matter by Delhi police also indicates that there is prima facie no substance in the allegation that Shri Jal Singh committed suicide on 21.05.2000 because he was harassed by the CBI.

MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( SHRI JAGMOHAN )


(a)&(b): Government have not received any order issued by the Supreme Court/High Court to regularise illegal constructions and encroachments. Action against illegal constructions and encroachments is taken as per the relevant laws. records.qtitle: PRIVATISATION OF AIR
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to privatize All India Radio;

(b) if so, the reasons behind privatizing such a sensitive agency like All India Radio; and

(c) if not, the reaction and decision of Government with regard to the newsitem published in the Hindustan, dated 2nd June, 2000 with regard to radio transmission?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING AND THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW, JUSTICE & COMPANY AFFAIRS (SHRI ARUN JAITLEY)




(a) No, Sir.

(b) Does not arise.

(c) The newspaper report refers to issue of FM Radio licences to private agencies. The Government have decided to allow 100% Indian owned companies to set up 108 FM Radio Stations in 40 cities in the first phase, which will supplement and not replace the services being provided by All India Radio. The basic objective behind licencing the private FM Stations is to give radio listeners more choice by making available more programmes with localized flavour in terms of content and relevance, in addition to generating employment opportunity by bringing the private sector resources to the Radio broadcasting sector.

records.qtitle: INCREASE IN IMPORT DUTY ON EDIBLE OIL H .
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the representatives from edible oil industry have demanded increase in import duty on edible oil;

(b) if so, whether Government have taken or propose to take any decision on the said demand; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefore and what will be its effect on the oil producers in the country if the import duty is not increased?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY ( SHRI MURASOLI MARAN)

(a) to (c) Based on representations received from edible oil industry and from growers of oil seeds, the customs duty on import of edible has been increased on 12.6.2000.
The total duty of customs on `Edible grade crude vegetable oils (excluding coconut oil, palm oil and its fractions whether refined or not ) imported in loose or bulk form for the manufacture of vanaspati or for refining` has been increased form 16.5 % to 27.5%, the duty on `Refined vegetable oils ( other than coconut oil , RBD palm oil, RBD palm kernel oil and palm stearin ) of edible grade in loose or bulk form` has been increased from 32.6% to 44.04%. Similarly the duty on `Coconut oil and Refined palm oil` has been increased from 44.04% to 50.8% .

records.qtitle: (clubbed) RECONSIDERATION OF DECISION REGARDING FREE TELEPHONE .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether attention of government has been drawn to news item captioned `Muft Phone Ka Vit Mantri Ne Virodh Kiya, Sanchar Ayog Ne Manzoori Di` published in the Nav Bharat Times dated the 8th June, 2000;

(b) whether free telephones to employees in Telecom Department and Telecom Services Department have been sanctioned;

(c) the loss of revenue;

(d) whether the Cabinet would reconsider and withdraw such facilities limited to a particular class of particular Department; and

(e) if not, the reasons not to give such facilities to all Central Government employees? ................
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS (SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR)

(a) Sir, Government is aware of the various news items appearing in the newspapers against the decision of Department to provide the concessional telephone facility to the serving employees of DoT.

(b) No Sir.

(c) Estimated recurring loss of revenue will be between Rs. 78.30 crore (for Low Calling) to Rs. 99.90 crore(for High Calling) per annum. Most of them are likely to fall under low calling subscriber category. As such, the implications are likely to be to the extent of Rs. 78.30 crore. In addition to this, non-recurring loss would be Rs. 24 Crore on account of installation charges.

(d) & (e) There is no proposal to refer the matter to the Cabinet. The decision has been taken by the Telecom Commission. Which is competent for this purpose under the executive and financial powers vested in it. This decision has been taken in the wake of increased competitive environment which has emerged in the telecom sector. The decision is meant to motivate its employees and increase their availability. It is thus an operational decision taken by the Telecom Commission and therefore it does not impact other Departments. However, formal orders for implementation of this scheme have not been issued so far in view of the interim stay given by Kerala High Court. ............

records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
e:-

(a) whether Government had constituted any Expert Committee for bringing about improvements in Prasar Bharati;

(b) if so, whether the said Committee has submitted its report to Government;

(c) if so, what are the suggestions of the Committee and whether Government are in full agreement with the suggestions of the Committee and want to implement it in its original form; and

(d) if so, by when and if not, the reasons therefor and the advantage of constituting the Committee?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING AND MINISTER OF STATE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DISINVESTMENT (SHRI ARUN JAITLEY)





(a) to (d): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.


………………





STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 63 FOR ANSWER ON 24.7.2000



(a) to (d) : The Government had constituted a Committee comprising of Shri N.R. Narayanamurthy, CEO Infosys, Shri Kiran Karnik, MD, Discovery Communications India and Shri Shunu Sen, a well known Marketing Consultant to study the working of Prasar Bharati and keeping in view its responsibility as a public service broadcaster to make appropriate recommendations with regard to its organizational structure, legal framework, systems and other relevant areas to ensure quality, credibility and professionalism within the organization. The committee has submitted its report on 20th May, 2000. The recommendations/suggestions of the Committee, amongst others, include mission and objective for Prasar Bharati, accountability and structures of Prasar Bharati, financing and funding mechanism, channel positioning, programming content and production, restructuring of transmission and engineering services, improvement in marketing, human resource development and exploitation of new technologies. The recommendations also contain certain amendments in the Prasar Bharati Act, 1990. A copy of the report is available at Ministry`s website i.e. mib.nic.in. View on some of the recommendations of the Committee is to be taken by Prasar Bharati, where as in respect of some others, Government has to take a view. The Government is in the process of consulting the members of the Prasar Bharati Board, representatives of staff and employees unions before taking a final view. The report has also been circulated among the Members of the Consultative Committee to seek their views.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) REHABILITATION OF CHILD LABOUR .
records.name: Ramdas Agarwal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received a report entitled `Child Labour, Education and Rehabilitation` submitted by the Centre of Concern for Child Labour as reported in the Hindustan Times on the 4th April, 2000;

(b) if so, whether it is a fact that only 4 lakh children in hazardous employment are rehabilitated as against promise to rehabilitate two million children in 2000;

(c) whether as per Ministry of Labour record there were 44 million child workers in 1991, if so, what is the number thereof at present in the country; and

(d) what are Government`s concrete plans for their rehabilitation during the year 2000-2001?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT ( SHRI MUNI LALL )

(a) to (d) : Centre of Concern for Child Labour has submitted a report to the Government in April, 2000. The report inter-alia, contains details on definition of Child Labour, extent of child labour, types of child labour, Government of India`s Policy towards child labour, rehabilitation of child labour through different models and challenges for future. Authentic information on Child Labour is generated during the decennial Census. As per the 1991 census, the total number of working children in the country is 11.28 million. Government of India has been implementing two schemes, for rehabilitation of Children withdrawn from work, namely the scheme of National Child Labour Projects (NCLP) and the scheme of Grant-in-aid to Voluntary Organisations. 92 NCLPs are currently under implementation in 10 child labour endemic states for rehabilitation of 1.9 lakh children. Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs ( CCEA )in its meeting held on 20.1.99 approved the continuance of the scheme of NCLP for the duration of the Ninth Plan and expansion of number of projects to 100. Under the Scheme of Grant-in-aid, funds are released to Voluntary Organisations, on the recommendation of the concerned State Government, for taking up action oriented projects for the benefit of working children. Over 70 projects are currently under implementation under the Scheme of grant-in-aid.
The above Schemes are continuing in the year 2000-2001 also.
Government is committed to the goal of eradication of child labour in all its forms. Considering the nature and magnitude of the problem a gradual, progressive and sequential approach has been adopted to withdraw and rehabilitate child labour.

records.qtitle: RISE IN CRIME DUE TO INFILTRATION .
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a) the reaction of Government on the news-item captioned `Sakht Qanoono Ke Karan Pak Nahin Jaate Bangladeshi` appearing in the `Dainik Jagaran` dated 10th March, 2000; and

(b) the steps Government are contemplating to take in order to check incidents of prostitutiion and other crimes which are on the rise due to foreign infiltrators ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HOME AFFAIRS ( SHRI L.K. ADVANI )

(a): In view of the long and porous border with Bangladesh and also on account of various push and pull factors, many Bangladeshis have managed to sneak into various parts of the country. Due to ethnic and linguistic similarities, they are able to mingle easily with the local population.
As per available reports, some Bangladeshi immigrants cross over to Pakistan in search of better livelihood. About 3846 Bangladeshi infiltrators have been apprehended along the Indo-Pak border since 1997 (till March 2000).
Various measures have been taken to check infiltration. These include, inter alia, construction of border roads, border fencing, raising of additional battalions of the Border Security Force, intensification of patrolling along the border, increase in the number of outpost towers, provision of surveillance equipment including night vision devices, etc. The matter has also been taken up with the Government of Bangladesh at various levels from time to time. There are standing instructions to the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations to detect and deport foreigners staying illegally.

(b): Instructions have been issued to the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations to deal firmly with those found violating the law of the land.

(c) if so, whether government had approved its proposal;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER

( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )

(a) to (e) : National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) received two bids under International Competitive Bidding (ICB) for Main Plant Package for Stage-II of Kavas and Gandhar power projects in Gujarat. Both the bidders did not meet qualifying requirements relating to Joint Deed of Undertaking and took major deviations on various specifications, operational functional guarantees, completion schedule and other important conditions of the bid rendering the bids non-responsive.
Keeping in view national importance of these projects and for ensuring their timely completion during the Ninth Plan period, NTPC was advised by the Ministry in the public interest to finalise the bids by negotiating with the bidders on the basis of a legal opinion taken from the Additional Solicitor General. However, NTPC, taking into account certain major deviations on various specifications and requirements, treated both the bids as non-responsive and decided to rebid. Government has left the matter to the NTPC Board being a Navratna Company for a decision. A review of bidding conditions has been undertaken by NTPC and rebidding is being done by providing adequate time to the bidders for better competition and response.

All steps are taken to further streamline the procurement process and to minimise the time taken in decision making. A committee has been set up under the Chairmanship of Vice Chief of Army Staff to examine the existing Defence Procurement Procedures in their entirety with a view to suggest specific measures for speedier processing of acquisition cases.

records.qtitle: SECURITY PERSONNEL KILLED BY LANDMINE BLAST .
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:

(b) the steps taken by Government to curb completely such incidents which are taking place continuously ; and

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI L.K. ADVANI)


(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.



STATEMENT AS REFERRED TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 296 FOR ANSWER ON 15.3.2000.

(a)to(c): No Statewise record regarding the number of security and police personnel killed in landmine blasts, is maintained by the Central Government . However, the Government of India and the concerned State Governments continuously review the situation arising out of militancy, terrorism, insurgency and extremist activities.
In order to tackle cross-border terrorism in Jammu & Kashmir, Government of India has implemented an action plan. For neutralising militancy / terrorism in the North-East various steps including deployment of CPMFs and Army, improved coordination and intelligence sharing between security forces, modernisation/upgradation of State Police Forces etc. have been undertaken.
For effectively countering Left Wing Extremism, the affected States of Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Orissa were requested to prepare integrated action plans encompassing the development as well as security aspects of the problem for the affected areas. The States have also been advised to take vigorous follow-up action. The Government of India has also set up a coordination centre headed by the Union Home Secretary with Chief Secretaries and Directors General of Police of the States affected by Left Wing Extremism, as its members, to review steps taken to check the Left Wing Extremist activities, monitor the plan of action in respect of each state etc.
In addition, in order to minimise attacks due to landmine and / or IED blasts on security forces/police personnel/civilians, steps such as deployment of road opening parties, use of metal detectors, mine protected vehicles etc. are being taken.

MINISTER OF STATE OF DEPARTMENT OF (SMT. VASUNDHARA RAJE) PERSONNEL AND TRAINING AND DEPARTMENT OF PENSION AND PENSIONERS` WELFARE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS.

(a), (b), (c) and (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

.PA STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN PARTS (a), (b), (c) AND (d) OF RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2399 SLATED FOR 23.12.1999 REGARDING APPOINTMENT OF SUCCESSFUL OBC CANDIDATES


(a), (b), (c) & (d) : Union Public Service Commission

(hereinafter referred to as UPSC) had recommended a total of 215 candidates belonging to Other Backward Classes (OBCs) for appointment on the basis of the Civil Services Examination (CSE) 1997 : of these, 166 candidates had been recommended by relaxed standards for the 166 vacancies reserved for OBCs, whereas 49 candidates belonging to OBC category were recommended as part of the list of general category candidates as they had qualified the CSE 1997 without availing any of the concessions/relaxations available for the OBCs.
The combined order of merit declared by UPSC forms the basis of service allocation to 28 different services/posts having regard to the position in order of merit, order of preference for the available services, category-wise vacancy, status on medical fitness and previous employment. In the course of allocation of service, it was found that out of the 49 OBC candidates, who had been recommended as part of the list of the general category candidates, only two could be allocated to a service of their higher preference without availing the benefit of reservation for purposes of service allocation and were, as such, adjusted against unreserved vacancies. The remaining 47 candidates, however, who could be allocated to the service of their higher preference only through relaxed standards for purposes of service allocation were given the benefit of reservation for the purpose of allocation to a service of their higher preference and, hence, were adjusted against OBC vacancies in that service. As such, there were 213 (166+47) OBC candidates available for allocation to the 166 reserved vacancies for the OBCs. Of these 213 OBC candidates -

(a) 166 OBC candidates were allocated to various services;

(b) 30 OBC candidates were ineligible for allocation as they either had already accepted allocation to a service on the basis of an earlier Civil Services Examination and had not qualified for allocation to services/posts which were higher in the order of preference as per Rule 18 of the CSE, 1997 Rules, or were declared physically unfit by Medical Board for appointment;

(c) the remaining 17 OBC candidates could not be allocated to a service on the basis of CSE 1997 due to the non-availability of vacancy at their turn in the merit order under the OBC category.

3. The manner of service allocation followed by the Government is strictly in accordance with the ratio laid down by the Hon`ble Supreme Court in the case of Ritesh R.Shah (JT 1996

(2) SC 495); M. Neethi Chandra (1996 6 SCC 36) and Dr. Anil Kumar (1998 9 SCC 405). Some of the recommended OBC candidates who could not be allocated to a service also agitated the matter before CAT Hyderabad Bench (A. Murali Manohan and N. Vijay Bhaskar) and CAT Principal bench (Satya Prakash and Anil Kumar) and both the benches of the CAT upheld the manner of service allocation as followed by the Government.

The resolution of the boundary between India and China is outstanding. 2. The two sides have been discussing the boundary question in the framework of the Joint Working Group to seek a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable settlement of the boundary. Both sides have also reiterated their commitment to respect the Agreement on Maintenance of Peace and Tranquillity along the LAC in the India-China Border Areas and the Agreement on Confidence Building Measures in the Military Field for the maintenance of peace and tranquillity in the border areas.


3. Constant vigil is kept on our borders and all developments having a bearing on our national security are closely monitored. All necessary measures continue to be taken to maintain defence preparedness.

records.qtitle: INCLUSION OF INDIA IN THE LIST OF COUNTRIES MAKING NARCOTICS .
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have registered any protest or taken any action on the inclusion of India`s name by USA in the list of the countries making narcotics; and

(b) if so, USA`s reaction thereto? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI JASWANT SINGH)


(a) In November, the US Government presented Part I of its annual International Narcotics Control Strategy Report to the US Congress. The report is in pursuance of the US Foreign Assistance Act 1996 on international efforts to meet the goals and objectives of the 1988 UN Convention Against Illicit Traffic in Narcotics and Psychotropic Substance.
Part I of the report is a simple listing of countries, which are either illicit drug producing or drug transit countries. With major drug producing countries in India`s neighbourhood, transit of drugs through India as a possibility is a source of concern, including to the Government of India. The Final Report, which was submitted to the US Congress in 1999, acknowledges that India has taken adequate steps on its own to achieve the objectives of the 1988 United Nations Convention.


(b) Does not arise

records.qn_text:

(d) whether Government intend to check killing of tigers and take action against the persons involved in their killing and smuggling; and

(e) if so, the details and the time-frame therefor ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT & FORESTS

(SHRI BABULAL MARANDI)

(a)&(b) It is a fact that incidents of tiger poaching for illegal trade of tiger parts in the foreign countries have come to the notice of the Government.

(c) The number of tiger poaching cases as detected and reported by the States are as under: - Year 1991 1992 1993 1994 1995 1996 1997 1998 Poaching cases 7 8 17 18 5 6 4 6

(d)&(e) Yes, Sir. Poachers and smugglers are prosecuted under the Wildlife

(Protection) Act which prescribes imprisonment of one to six years and also a minimum fine ofRs.5000/-. Besides, Government has taken several effective measures to control tiger poaching and smuggling of its body parts which are given in the Annexure. ANNEXURE ANNEXURB REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (d) & (e) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION N0.1886 ON `KILLINGS OF TIGERS` BY PROF. RAM GOPAL YADAV AND SHRI ISH DUTT YADAV ON FRIDAY, THE 12TH MARCH. 1999. STEPS TAKEN BY THE GOVERNMENT OF INDIA TO PROTECT TIGER National Level:

1. Setting up of, a National Coordination Committee to control poaching and illegal trade in wildlife with enforcement agencies like Customs, Revenue Intelligence, Indo-Tibbetan Border Police, Border Security Force, Central Reserve Police Force, Coast Guards, State Police, Deputy Director, Wildlife Preservation & Scientific Organisations like Zoological and Botanical Survey of India.

2. Training programmes and Workshops have been organized to sensitize the above departments to be proactive in control of trade and smuggling of wildlife products.

3. A special co-ordination committee with. Secretary (E&F), Special Secretary

(Home), Director, CBI and representative of the Chairman, Central Board of Excise & Customs has been created to ensure better co-ordination in the efforts to curb smuggling of wildlife products.

4. Central assistance js being provided to State Governments to strengthen the protection infrastructure including armed squads, vehicles, communication network and co-ordination `between the Park managers. Government of India has earmarked approximately Rs.20 crores for this purpose.

5. Schemes for awards and rewards for outstanding performance and acts of valour has been introduced to encourage detection and reporting. 6. The State Governments have been advised to strengthen vigilance and intensify patrolling.

7 Launching of public awareness programme to involve Non-Governmental Organisations and others for supporting the Government in its efforts towards wildlife conservation. /

8. Supporting programmes of Institutions and NGOs in exploring tiger-trade routes and developing a forensic identification reference biannual for tiger parts and products.

9. Funds are being provided to the State Governments for the eco-development of the areas to reduce the biotic pressure thereon. 10. Site specific special force in Project Tiger Areas. International Level:

1. Initiated creation of a Forum of Tiger Range Countries, i.e. Global Tiger Forum for addressing international issues related to tiger conservation.

2. To control transboundary trade and effect mutual cooperation in tiger conservation: -
(i) A protocol has been signed with People`s Republic of China.
(ii) An MOU with His Majesty`s Government of Nepal has been signed.
(iii) Dialogue with Bangladesh has been initiated.

3. Several resolutions at CITES to check illegal trade in tiger parts and products have been adopted at India`s initiative.

records.qtitle: DISCUSSION WITH PAKISTAN ON THE NUCLEAR RESTRAINT
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government of Pakistan have proposed a discussion with India on the nuclear restraint,

(b) if so, the extensive details of the said proposal and whether Government have taken any step towards fixing the time and venue for a discussion on the proposal; and

(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, what stand has been taken by Government on the said proposal of Pakistan?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI JASWANT SINGH)

(a-c) As part of the composite dialogue process, India and Pakistan are holding discussions on Peace and Security, including Confidence Building Measures. During the first round of discussions on this subject, in October 1998, various proposals were exchanged, including proposals by Pakistan on nuclear restraint India drew Pakistan`s attention to our security needs which flow naturally from our size, location and assets and are not one country-specific. We also emphasised that our defence posture was non-aggressive. In this context, India proposed the upgradation of existing CBMs and the need to put into place new CBMs in the nuclear and conventional fields. Government have also declared that India shall maintain a credible minimum nuclear deterrent, pursue a no first use doctrine, observe a moratorium on farther nuclear test explosions and refrain from engaging in an arms race. India`s approach, therefore, is one of exemplary restraint and moderation. During the visit of Prime Minister to Pakistan on 20-21 February 1999, Prime Minister and the Prime Minister of Pakistan signed the Lahore Declaration in which it was agreed that the two countries would take immediate steps for reducing the risk of accidental or unauthorised use of nuclear weapons and discuss concepts and doctrines with a view to elaborating measures for confidence building in the nuclear and conventional fields, aimed at the prevention of conflict. On this occasion, a Memorandum of Understanding was also signed between the Foreign Secretaries of India and Pakistan under which both countries have Agreed to lake measures and conclude agreement wherever necessary to build confidence in the nuclear and conventional fields. It has also been agreed in the Memorandum of Understanding that the technical details will be worked out by experts of the two sides in meetings to be held on mutually agreed dates before mid`99.

records.qtitle: REASONS FOR INFILTRATION OF BANGLADESHIS .
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a.) the year-wise number of infiltrations by the Bangladeshis into India., together the number of such infiltrators estimated during 1999;

(b) the reasons for the continuing infiltration of Bangladeshis into India; and

(c) the action being contemplated by Government in the areas along Bangladesh border to step such infiltration?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI L.K. ADVANI)

(a) It is difficult to make an estimate of the number of infiltrators from Bangladesh because they enter surreptitiously and are able to mingle easily with the local population due to ethnic and linguistic similarities.

(b) Ethnic proximity, porous and easily negotiable border, Better economic opportunities in India and sharp deterioration in land-man ratio in Bangladesh are some of. the factors responsible for continuing infiltration of Bangladeshi nationals into India.

(c): A series of measures have been taken by the Government to curb the problem of infiltration of Bangladesh nationals into India. These measures include raising of additional battalions of Border Security Force, reduction of gaps between the broder outposts, intensification of patrolling both on the land and the riverine border, accelerate programme of constraction of Border roads and fencing, increase in the number of outpost towere, provision of surveillance equipments etc. The matter has also been taken up with the Government of Bangladesh on various occasions. The progress of these measures is reviewed regularly at various levels.

THE MINISTER OF LABOUR (DR. SATYANARAYAN JATIYA)

(a) to (d): Necessary rules/guidelines already exist for providing prompt service to the EPF subscribers covered under the Employees Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952. records.qtitle: COMPULSORY EDUCATION TO THE. CHILDREN OF THE POOR .

MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT( DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI)

(a) to (c) : Government is aware that children from poor families often find it difficult to sand their children to school regularly due to social-economic constraints. records.qtitle: SPECIAL ENTRY PASSES FOR MINISTRIES .
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a) whether there is any criteria/procedure for issuing special passes by the Ministry for entering offices of different Ministries; if so what is that procedure and whether it is being complied with;

(b) whether it is a fact that no action has been taken despite gross irregularities in issuing these passes having come into notice;

(c) if so, the details of officials responsible therefor;

(d) whether hundreds of employees of Secretariat security force have sought justice from the Home Minister against the autocratic approach of certain top level officers;

(e) if so, the action taken by Government to do justice to them?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF HOME AFFAIRS ( SHRI L.K. ADVAMI )

(a) Photo passes are issued for entry to Government buildings under the security cover of the Ministry of Home Affairs (except a few building under special security cover) in accordance with the following criteria and procedure.
(i) Open photo passes are issued to gazetted officers on application made in the prescribed proforma, duly sponsored by the concerned Ministries/Departments.
(ii) Restricted photo passes, for specified buildings, are issued to non-gazetted officials on application made in the prescribed proforma, duly sponsored by the concerned Ministries/Departments. However, in a few cases, non-gazetted officials are issued open passes based on functional requirements, on the specific recommendation of the sponsoring Ministries/Departments. R.S. USQ NO. 194 for 24.
(iii) State Government officials and officials of the undertakings/corporations of the Government are issued open or restricted photo passes, depending on the justification given, on application made in the prescribed proforma, duly sponsored by the concerned State governments or the administrative Ministries/Departments, as the case may be.
(iv) Certain casual employees engaged/employed by service agencies like CPWD; MTNL, etc. are also issued passes, depending on the functional requirement, on the sponsership of the concerned agencies.
(v) Certain non-officials are selectively issued open or restricted passes, again depending on the functional requirement, on the merit of each case.
(vi) Entry of visitors to Government buildings is regulated through visitors` passes issued by the deception Organisation of the Secretariat Security Organisation, The procedures prescribed for issue of passes to various categories of persons mentioned above are being complied with.

(b) & (c) No such irregularities in issuing these passes have come to notice.

(d) A section of employees of the Secretariat Security Force has not taken kindly to certain instructions issued by the Secretariat Security Organisation aimed at enforcing discipline in the organisation and has made complaint against some officials. The Chief Security Officer has been instructed to hear the grievances of the employees once a week and take appropriate action for the redressal of their legitimate grievances. The employees can also meet senior officials of the Ministry for redressal of their grievances.

records.qtitle: TRADE BETWEEN INDIA AND PAKISTAN
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any discussion had taken place between India and Pakistan for increasing trade and commercial cooperation;

(b) if so, the outcome thereof; (

(c) whether Pakistan are purchasing several items f ID m other countries other than India despite the above talks;

(d) if so, the names of those items and the reasons therefor; and

(e) the steps Government are considering to take to ensure promotion of trade and commercial cooperation between India and Pakistan?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF COMMERCE ( SHRI RAMAKRISHNA HEGDE)

(a) Yes. Sir.

(b) Commerce Secretary level talks between India and Pakistan on Economic and Commercial Cooperation were held in New Delhi on 10th November`98. Both sides i.e. India and Pakistan exchanged ideas on issues affecting bilateral trade, A series of steps aimed at enhancing the scope of cooperation were discussed. The Indian delectation inter-alia pointed out that while India has already accorded Most Favoured Nation(MFN) status to Pakistan since the 1970s, Pakistan is yet to grant similar status to India in accordance with its obligations under GATT/WTO. The Pakistan delegation assured that they would fulfil their obligation in `due course`. During the discussions, it was agreed that the technical teams on Railways and Power from India and Pakistan would meet for detailed discussions in these areas. Both sides agreed to have regular consultations on issues relating to social clause, environment etc. to have common approach.

(c)&(d): Pakistan currently allows import of only 594 items from India which include items like fresh vegetables, pulses, coffee»tea, spices, oil seeds, edible vegetable oils, soybean meal, inorganic and organic chemicals, pharmaceutical raw materials, tyres & tubes, cotton and cotton yarn, raw or processed jute, waste/scrap metal, metal and its products, engineering and machinery items etc. During the discussions, the Indian delegation suggested that the list of-goods to be imported from India be expanded. So far, there has not been any addition to their list of items importable from India.

(e) It would be the endevour of the Government to continue the dialogue process with Pakistan for promotion of trade and commercial cooperation between the two countries and also by exchanging business delegations and participating in Trade Fairs etc.

The green revolution in aggregative terms has resulted in higher employment in agriculture.

records.qtitle: TALKS WITH USA .
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any talks were held between a special representative of Government of India and Deputy Secretary of State of United States of America in the third week of August;

(b) If so, the date and venue thereof, togetherwith the number of rounds of talks;

(c) the details and outcome of the said talks togetherwith the reaction of Government of India to the same; and

(d) the details of further talks proposed with US and the progress thereon, so far?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI JASWANT SINGH)

(a) We have been engaged in an ongoing dialogue with the United States since June, 1998. The dialogue is being conducted through Shri Jaswant Singh, Deputy Chairman, Planning Commission and Mr.Strobe Talbott, US Deputy Secretary of State. Six rounds of talks have been held so far. Fourth round of talks was held in the third week of August.

(b) The talks were held from August 20-21, in Washington. There was also a brief follow-up meeting in New York on-August 29, 1998.

(c) The talks are being conducted on the basis of the comprehensive proposals that India has put forward on disarmament and non-proliferation matters comprising our unilateral moratorium on explosive nuclear tests, our willingness to discuss converting this moratorium into a de jure obligation, our offer to enter into constructive negotiations on the FMCT and our determination to make more stringent the existing system of export controls over sensitive material and technology. The dialogue has resulted in some progress. India has firmly conveyed its security concerns as well as the need for India to-maintain a minimum credible nuclear deterrent. These talks are predicated on this basis. There now exists some understanding for India`s concerns and requirements. After six rounds, the talks have narrowed, and are now focussed on four issues, which are mainly centered around the proposals which India had initially put forward. These issues are the CTBT, the FMCT, Export Controls and Defence Posture.

(d) Two more rounds of talks were held after August 1998, -in September (21) and November(19-20), in Washington and Rome respectively. In addition, an expert-level meeting was also held on the subject of Export Controls in New Delhi on 9-10 November, 1998 as a part of the ongoing dialogue. Both sides have agreed to meet in the second half of January, 1999 in New Delhi to carry forward this process.

records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that due to replacement of Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) by the Foreign Exchange Management Act, !998 (FEMA) the morale of those involved in the embezzlement of foreign exchange has become high and it will result in more cases of embezzlement of foreign exchange;

(b) whether it is also a fact that `sensitive` and `very sensitive` cases will be examined under FEMA; and

(c) if not, the way in which Government propose to check the embezzlement of foreign exchange by taking action against the persons involved therein and to examine the sensitive and very sensitive cases.
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI YASHWANT SINHA)

(a) : No, Sir.

(b) & (c) : The cases of embezzlement are dealt with under the normal criminal laws and that even under the existing FERA, 1973 and the proposed FEM Bill, 1998 there does not exist any provision to tackle and take care of the aspect of embezzlement of foreign exchange. Further, the violations/contraventions committed after coming into force of FEMA would be governed by the provisions of FEMA. Even though FERA is repealed when FEMA comes into force: Clause 49(3)(a) of FEM Bill provides that offences/contraventions of repealed Act committed during the currency of that Act would be governed by the provisions of the repealed Act as if that Act has not been repealed. Thus as per the existing provisions of the Bill, cases of contraventions whether `sensitive` or `very sensitive` committed during the currency of FERA would be governed by the provisions of FERA and those committed when FEMA comes into force will be governed by the provisions of FEMA.

records.qn_text:

(b) whether the Supreme Court has upheld the claim of reimbursement of medical expenses, in toto, incurred by a retired Central Government employee;

(c) if so, whether Government are considering to implement the decision of the apax Court be extending medical facilities to retired Government employees living in the area outside the jurisdiction of CGHS and making them eligible for reimbursement of such expenses;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY): (a) and (b) Based on the facts of the case of an employee of the Govt. of Punjab, the Supreme Court has held that `it is but the duty of the State of bear the expenditure incurred by the Govt. servant. Expenditure, thus, incurred requires to be reimbursed by the State to the employee`. The court has further observed that `having had the constitutional obligation to bear the expenses for the Govt. Servant while in service or after retirement from service, as per the policy of the Govt. the Govt. is required to fulfil the constitutional obligation. Necessarily, the State has to bear the expenses incurred in that behalf`.

(c) to (e) As per existing Rules, the serving Central Govt. employees are extended medical facilities either under CGHS or under CS(MA) Rules. The pensioners are covered only under CGHS. The Fifth Central Pay Commission, in its Report, has recommended extension of CS(MA) Rules, 1944, to pensioners, not covered under CGHS, in a restricted manner `so as to facilitate reimbursement of expenditure on hospitalisation in a Govt. hospital/private hospital recognised under CGHS or under CS(MA) Rules for the purpose`. This proposal is under examination of the Government.

records.qtitle: INSTALLATION OF STATE OF MAHATMA GANDHI AT INDIA GATE .
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to clear the confusion about installation of the statue of Mahatma Gandhi at India Gate; and

(b) whether the matter has been inordinately delayed?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN AFFAIRS & EMPLOYMENT AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS (DR. V.VENKATESWARLU)

(a) and (b) The Government`s commitment to install the statue of Mahatma Gandhi at India Gate or at any other suitable location in Delhi remains. The Government is at present considering the suitability of different locations at the India Gate Complex as well as outside it for installation of the statue during 50th year of India`s independence. However, the matter is subjudice in the Delhi High Court which had issued an interim order in CWP No. 2725/95 restricting the Government of India from ` Alering/removing/demolishing the Canopy/Chatri at the India Gate roundabout renamed as August Kranti udyan`.

records.qtitle: FUDGING OF STC ACCOUNTS .
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government`s attention has been drawn to the news item published in Financial Express of October 1, 1996, regarding fudging of STC accounts;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) in what way Government propose to cover up Rs. 51 crores loss suffered by corporation?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE (SHRI BOLLA BULI RAMAIAH)

(a) Yes, sir.

(b) and (c) state Trading Corporation of India has intimated that it finalized its accounts for the financial year 1995-96 on the basis of its well established accounting policies. The accounts were audited by the statutory auditors appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General and the same were considered and approved by the Board of Directors of STC. These audited accounts of STC reflected a profit of Rs. 32.67 crores. However, C&AG subsequently in its comments observed that the provision should be made for the following amounts:-

(a) Rs.20.02 crores to be realized on account of canalized import of newsprint in the period prior & upto 1991-92.

(b) Rs. 60.33 crores to be realized on account of import of fatty acid.

(c) Rs. 3.00 crores as investment made in Tea Trading corporation of India (TTCI), a wholly owned subsidiary of STC.
The Board of Directors of STC considered the comments and keeping in view the facts that the amounts at (a) & (b) above are debts to be realized from the Government and sale of tea gardens is under process in TTCI, the BOARD decided not to make any provision for these amounts. The shareholders of STC in the Annual General Meeting also approved the stand taken by STC Board.

(a) and (b) Rajghat, the samadhi of Mahatma Gandhi is governed by the Rajgaht Samadhi Act ,1951 and rules made thereunder . NO such Act has been passed by the Parliament in repect of Samadhis of Pandit Jawahar Lal Nehru or any other Prime Minister located in Delhi. NO violation of such statue hes been brought to the notice of the Central Government . However ,some portion of the land with the Rajghat Samadhi Committee was allotted in 1984 , with the consent of the committee for the Samadhi of Smt . Indira Gandhi . records.qtitle: EFFECT OF GANGA WATER TREATY ON CALCUTTA PORT .
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the recent Ganga Water sharing treaty with Bangladesh would spell disaster for the Calcutta port;

(b) whether Government propose to maintain guaranteed supply of Water for Calcutta port during the months from January to May;

(c) whether Bangladesh and India would benefit keeping in view the fact that the flow of water in the river had gone down recently; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA):

(a) No, Sir.

(b) Sharing of the Ganga/Ganges waters at Farakka by 10 day periods from 1st January to 31st May every year will be with reference to the formula in the Treaty.

(c) and (d) The Treaty is expected to benefit both the countries. The sharing arrangement under the Treaty shall be reviewed by the two Governments at Five Years interval or earlier as required by either party and needed adjustments, based on principles of equity, fairness and no harm together party made thereto, if necessary. It would be open to either party to seek the first review after two years to assess the impact and working of the sharing arrangement. Thus appraisal of work-ability and flows will be possible after Joint Observations are carried out for two years.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) RECOMMENDATIONS OF ABID HUSSAIN COMMITTEE ON SMALL ENTERPRISES .
records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received the report of Abid Hussain Committee;

(b) if so, whether abolition of the present reservation system in the sector of small scale industries has been suggested in the report;

(c) the main recommendations of the Committee`s report;

(d) whether the Government have since considered the recommendations of the report; and

(e) if so, decision taken by Government in this regard and if no decision has been taken, by when it will be taken?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF INDUSTRY (SHRI MURASOLI MARAN)

(a) and (b) Yes, Sir.

(c) to (e) In addition to the recommendation for abolition of reservation of products for exclusive manufacture in the SSI Sector, major recommendations of the Abid Hussain Committee relate to raising the investment limit for SSI Sector, mechanism for promotion of small scale industries, focus on clusters, restructuring financial support for SSI Sector, integrated support services, support for technology development in small scale enterprises, infrastructure development in clusters and institutional and legal innovations and revitalising the District Industry Centers. Recommendations made by the Committee are being examined in consultations with relevant Ministries/Departments etc. After the receipt of the report, Government has already decided to raise the investment limit for plant & machinery in a SSI unit from Rs. 60/75 lakhs to Rs. 3 crores and that for a tiny unit from Rs. 5 lakhs to Rs. 25 lakhs, as recommended by the Committee. Earmarking a proper share of credit to the tiny sector within the priority sector lending is under active consideration of the Government for safeguarding their interest.

records.qtitle: ADDITION OF UNRESERVED COACHES IN THE TRAINS
records.name: Ram Gopal Yadav
records.qn_text:
(a) whether more unreserved coaches would be added in view of the heavy traffic in north-eastern railways;

(b) if so, what are the details thereof including the number of coaches likely to be added in each train; and

(c) if not, what are the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF RAILWAYS (SHRI C.K. JAFFER SHARIEF) :

(a) to (c) Depending upon traffic, operational feasibility and availability of coaches, additional unreserved coaches are provided on various sections and trains on N.E. Railway and this is a continuous process. In the July `95 Time Table, 2 pairs of `Janseva Express` trains with exclusive unreserved 2nd class accommodation between Bhagalpur and Muzafarpur and Amritsar and Barauni have been introduced. In addition, 4 pairs of trains have been introduced and the run of twenty existing trains has been extended on N.E. Railway system.
